title: annotated declarative mis-interprets Literal within Mapped[]

labels.name: PRs (with tests!) welcome
labels.description: a fix or feature which is appropriate to be implemented by volunteers

labels.name: orm - annotated declarative
labels.description: issues with the new annotations-based declarative ORM approach

body:
### Describe the bug

I get an `sqlalchemy.exc.ArgumentError: Could not resolve all types within mapped annotation: "Mapped[Status]"` error when I use `from __future__ import annotations` together with a `Mapped` column of type `typing.Literal`.

When I remove `from __future__ import annotations`, everything works as expected.

I'm aware that sqlalchemy already includes built-in support for `enum.Enum`. I'm aware that this is another workaround.

### To Reproduce

```python
# NOTE: Code works if we remove the following line
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Literal, Optional, get_args

import sqlalchemy.types as types
from sqlalchemy import Dialect
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column


class LiteralSqlType(types.TypeDecorator):
    impl = types.String
    cache_ok = True

    def __init__(self, literal_type: Any) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self._possible_values = get_args(literal_type)

    def process_bind_param(
        self, value: Optional[str], dialect: Dialect
    ) -> Optional[str]:
        if value not in self._possible_values:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid literal value '{value}'. Value must be one of"
                f" {self._possible_values}."
            )
        return value


Status = Literal["to-do", "in-progress", "done"]


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


class Foo(Base):
    __tablename__ = "foo"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    status: Mapped[Status] = mapped_column(None, LiteralSqlType(Status))
```

### Versions

- OS: `Linux 6f5cb13b6c98 5.15.0-46-generic #49~20.04.1-Ubuntu SMP Thu Aug 4 19:15:44 UTC 2022 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux`
- Python: `Python 3.10.9`
- SQLAlchemy: `sqlalchemy 2.0.0` (as released a couple of days ago)
- Database: N/A
- DBAPI (eg: psycopg, cx_oracle, mysqlclient): N/A


### Additional context

# My understanding of the issue

With `from __future__ import annotations`, python automatically converts all annotations to strings (simplified explanation). This makes it easier to use types out of declaration order. In turn, libraries that use annotations must "de-stringify" the annotations first. This last part is where I think the bug is at.

I think that sqlalchemy is too aggressive with it's "de-stringify annotations" logic.
First, sqlalchemy de-stringifies the literal itself: `'Literal["to-do", "in-progress", "done"]'` becomes `Literal["to-do", "in-progress", "done"]`. So far so good!
Second, sqlalchemy notices that `Literal` is generic (has arguments) and therefore attempts to recursively de-stringify each argument ("to-do", "in-progress", and "done"). However, these arguments are *not* annotations but mere strings. This causes the error.

# Patch to fix the issue

Change the `de_stringify_annotation` function in `sqlalchemy/util/typing.py` so that it explicitly accounts for the `typing.Literal` case:
Specifically, change the recursive part from:

```python
    if include_generic and is_generic(annotation):
        elements = tuple(
            de_stringify_annotation(
                cls,
                elem,
                originating_module,
                str_cleanup_fn=str_cleanup_fn,
                include_generic=include_generic,
            )
            for elem in annotation.__args__
        )

        return _copy_generic_annotation_with(annotation, elements)
    return annotation  # type: ignore
```

to:

```python
    is_literal = get_origin(annotation) is Literal
    if include_generic and is_generic(annotation) and not is_literal:
        elements = tuple(
            de_stringify_annotation(
                cls,
                elem,
                originating_module,
                str_cleanup_fn=str_cleanup_fn,
                include_generic=include_generic,
            )
            for elem in annotation.__args__
        )

        return _copy_generic_annotation_with(annotation, elements)
    return annotation  # type: ignore
```

The code works as expected (no errors) with this fix applied.

Let me know if you have any questions.

*Side note*: Version 2.0 of sqlalchemy is amazing. Great job!
